criteria.text: An app.Upload streams to storage, and a body over the api's max_upload gets 413 before it is read.

criteria.text: Storage names each stored file itself and returns a blob ID. The client's file name is kept only as metadata and never becomes part of a path, so a name such as ../../etc/passwd stores safely. The server checks the media type from the bytes against the declared list, and a body declared image/png that holds HTML gets 415.

criteria.text: Before it reads the body, attach runs the method that #App.UploadCheck(method:) names, as the caller and after the session check; that method applies the project's row policy (D-DBPOLICY1, #3709), so a signed-in caller who is not a member gets 403 and the body is never read.
criteria.evidence: p226 batch compiler (dev 713d2cd072; uploads 33b4f0a1d8 + 46177eada7): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/upload_by_a_non_member_is_403_before_it_is_read PASS (in WebApp/upload_ 3/3).

criteria.text: A download of a stored blob runs the read policy of the row that holds its BlobID and is served with Content-Disposition: attachment and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.
criteria.evidence: p226 batch compiler (dev 713d2cd072; uploads 33b4f0a1d8 + 46177eada7): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter WebApp/blob_download_runs_row_policy PASS 1/1.

criteria.text: An upload is spooled after its check passes and before the transaction starts; a retried transaction reads the staged body; a blob kept in a transaction that rolls back is deleted. A staged file lives no longer than its request, and one left by a crash is deleted when the server next starts.

cards.title: Compile-time evaluation: #run values match run time, fall back cleanly and run once
cards.body:
Destination: compile-time evaluation (`#run`, `#if`, `#loop`, `NAME: #run value`, and automatic folding of immutable bindings) means exactly what the same code means at run time, reports every failure at its source with a registered code, and never runs twice. Why: compile-time code is ordinary Jet; any drift between the two meanings is a silent wrong answer.

Governing decisions: D-META-SPELL1=A (`#run`, `#if`, `#loop` replace `comptime`; shipped, cases ratified_p12/d_meta_spell1_forms), D-COMPTIME-WORD1=A, D-PREP-BRANCH1=A, D-PREP-FN1=A, D-MODULE-BUILD1=A (a module-level value that fails or has effects is a build error, E0643), D-EXEC2=A (tiers are O0, O1 and O2; no interpreter). Spec: Docs/spec/reference/metaprogramming.md; the 2026-10-29 and 2026-11-10 entries of Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md.

Carried from #4276 (closed 2026-11-14).

log.text: All criteria met; c11 on p235 (dev 1c5b311279). The DMA clause of c14 lives on #6518 c8. One parser unit-test interaction with accept3 (a_trait_takes_type_parameters...) is with IfHole on #6857.

n14 (c), the registered #run stop for dma.start/dma.wait, is dropped from n14: DMA is unreachable on dev 78f4541780. No program reaches DMAStart/DMAWait: (1) sema needs a channel path from an imported `board.<profile>` module, and `use { sensor: board.sensor_v1 }` is E0603 whether board/ is a sibling directory or a dependency package; no repository fixture imports a `board.` module; (2) no shipped TargetMachine declares a DMA channel (hardware.dma_channels is empty for sensor_v1, virt_aarch64, wasm and hosted). A stop that no program reaches can have no I4 UI snapshot, so the comptime refusal (E3010 family) lands with the first reachable DMA path, in the same change that makes it reachable. Probe: PrecompiledCore-4 g7/n14/dma (E0603 output).

c16 (a) landed in p210 (7f6c05586e, 7f902dd915): by hand on the p210 gate tree, JET=<p210 jet> JETPACK_TEST_REPO_ROOT=<tree> jet test Jetpack/EnvModel/Tests/ModuleValueParity.jet passes 158 of 158. c16 stays open for (b): b1 is queued for p211, then b2-b7.

p209: c10 (06c5d8b172) ICEs: comptime_record_of_function_values exits 101 (ir.build unlowered: named function main.jet::double outside the checked program). PrecompiledCore-4 owns the fix (SUB PrecompiledCore-4-g6-c10-fix); c10 stays open.

c16 plan (Main): (a) EnvModel sends every immutable module value, with the source's functions and types, to the compiler in one request with source offsets kept. The compiler types them (field defaults included), orders them, reports cycles at the value span and gives E3410 and E0643; EnvModel drops its own graph, I/O gate and literal walk for module values. (b) EnvModel's schema walk over env, image and system record fields (EnvFields.jet:214-267, ComputedFields.jet:131-181) is a second typing of Jet literals. Its schema (Env, Lang, Prompt, Preset, package and lifecycle names) becomes Jet types in Jetpack/EnvModel source that the compiler checks record fields against; user syntax stays identical (jetpack-epoch5.md:503-506: the environment model owns typed projections). c16 is met only after (b).

Sweep of the open proofs on the p207 batch compiler (dev 0e93e25032), by Main. c5 met (FoldConstants o0/o1/o2 pass). n1: comptime_diff 161 pass, 0 fail, 3 known-failing (sequential_comptime_reads_advance_the_shared_reader, comptime_loadable_matches_runtime, loadable_incompatible_defaults_stop_before_rustc); open until those pass. n2, n3, n6, n7, n8, n13 and n14: their filters match no tests yet. n9: passes (comptime_loop_waits_on_named_constant); held for the run-value root loop follow-up queued for p209. n10: queued for p209. n11: waits on the generic-spelling ballot conflict. PrecompiledCore-4 order: n1, n7, n2, n3, n6, n8, n13, n14.

Owner-wait sweep 2026-11-15 (TowerKeeper-2, for Main): c11 reworded; the owner-only choices are on Main's ballot list (2026-11-15) ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/TowerKeeper-2/ballots-needed.tsv); no question for the owner stays on this card.

criteria.text: Run-time-only reflection, unsupported holes, unsafe raw use, an unknown DSL owner or type and mutable observations each fail at compile time with their registered diagnostic, and compile-time and run-time results agree: every comptime_diff case passes with none marked known-failing.
criteria.evidence: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter comptime_diff`: 164 rows, 0 failed, none known-failing. p210 batch compiler (dev 7f902dd915, census-clean build), proofs log $JET_STATE_ROOT/lander3-tmp/proofsp210.out

criteria.text: Self-cycles, longer cycles, missing or impure dependencies, invalid values and consumer disagreement among compile-time values each report the registered diagnostic at the owning source span, with UI snapshots.
criteria.evidence: `jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter comptime_dependency_`: 9 rows, 0 failed (including comptime_dependency_handle_value, E1018). p210 batch compiler (dev 7f902dd915, census-clean build), proofs log $JET_STATE_ROOT/lander3-tmp/proofsp210.out

criteria.text: An immutable `name: value` inside a block is computed while compiling whenever it can be and quietly falls back to run time for run-time inputs, outside effects, values that cannot be stored, or a step-limit stop; hover and `jet inspect` show the reason it fell back.
criteria.evidence: p216 batch compiler (census build of dev efb3da4f6c): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter comptime_fallback_reason PASS (3/3); ui runtime_only_called_while_building PASS

criteria.text: A compile-time fragment can call Core source functions through their loaded signatures (no E0956 'no loaded signature'), and a plain-literal constant registers without re-walking its unit, so registration time stays linear in unit size.
criteria.evidence: p206 batch compiler (dev fe8c7b89ef; landed as fe8c7b89ef, which also reverts the JetCli Core-assets workaround): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter comptime_core_call → PASS 1 FAIL 0 (p206 cycle proof row).

criteria.text: Every tier (O0, O1, O2) observes the same compile-time values and result, and a built binary never repeats compile-time work at startup.
criteria.evidence: jet test Compiler --profile golden --filter Metaprogramming/Comptime/FoldConstants on the p207 batch compiler (dev 0e93e25032): PASS Examples/Metaprogramming/Comptime/FoldConstants.jet o0, o1 and o2, rc 0 (rerun by Main; first reported by PrecompiledCore-4).

criteria.text: The NoEager policy turns off automatic compile-time evaluation but allows explicit `#run`; Only refuses compile-time execution of marked code; neither blocks ordinary optimizer folding.
criteria.evidence: p220 batch compiler (dev 17c073989d): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter comptime_policy_ PASS 3/3 (no_eager_keeps_explicit_run, keeps_optimizer_folding, only_refuses_compile_time_code)

criteria.text: `#run`, `#if`, `#loop` and `#run fn` never fall back silently to run time, never claim false purity and never execute a generated body before it is checked.
criteria.evidence: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter comptime_no_silent_fallback`: 4 rows, 0 failed; ui comptime_no_silent_fallback_run_fn_call (E1019) passes; goldens Metaprogramming/Comptime/PrepFn and tests/run/Foundations/Exact pass on O0, O1 and O2. p210 batch compiler (dev 7f902dd915, census-clean build), proofs log $JET_STATE_ROOT/lander3-tmp/proofsp210.out

criteria.text: `#run` executes ordinary code with no fallback stubs; persistent, session and effect lifetimes stay separate; native and process execution do not inherit host authority; a host/target mismatch is diagnosed before any effect runs.

cards.title: Browser tests in jet test: scaffold, UI mode, retry traces and cross-browser runs
cards.body:
Destination: `jet test` drives real browsers for an app: a scaffold sets up the browser test project, a UI mode shows one run in full, a retry records a trace you can open locally, and runs across browsers are deterministic and keep Jet's diagnostics and source positions.

Why it matters: end-to-end browser tests are where web apps break; parity with the best browser test runner (Playwright) is part of the web framework's parity bar.

Source: #6552 c15-c18 (from archived #2498 c2-c5). Parent: #6552.

cards.title: Close always runs exactly once: fields drop in order, and a Close during unwinding or cancellation follows the spec
cards.body:
Destination: every Close and #MustFinish value is released exactly once on every exit. Fields drop in the order D-FIELD-DROP-ORDER1=A sets, a second panic during unwinding stops the process as the spec says, and a cancel never cuts a running Close short.

Why: a Close that is skipped, runs twice or is cut short leaks a resource or corrupts its protocol (a file, a lock, a connection, a flush or a commit).

Source: map #5989 of the 2026-10-28 board consolidation. Its move and copy criteria went to #6923, purity check skipping to #3039, and region release to #6924. The known-failing row for the cancel case names this card.

log.text: Every criterion is met (criteria blocked on other cards were moved there with their work); closed under the closest-first order (2026-11-16).

Map split 2026-11-15 by TowerKeeper-1. This card keeps Close and drop order (c5, c17, c18). Moves and copies (c1, c2, c3, c4, c7, c10, c12, c13, c20) went to #6923, c14 to #3039 (PURESKIP), and c16 to #6924.
Owner deconfliction 2026-11-06: respelled for D-CALLSITE-MARK2=A (x.move() replaces ^x).

Merged #5041 "No implicit copies: native codegen and compiler source copy only where the source explicitly asks (.copy()), every copy justified" into this card (drop glue and moves: moves never copy, no implicit copies); its 5 open item(s) are carried as "(was #5041)" criteria. Owner ruling 2026-10-30: merge duplicate and superseded cards into one survivor.

Folded #5906 "A Close temporary passed to a borrowed parameter is never closed: sink(S { id: 5 }) skips close" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5989 (Map: Drop glue and moves: Close always runs,); 1 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Repro (fc382a23cd discovery jet, jet run): struct S { id: Int }, impl S.Close { fn close(^self) { print("close {self.id}") } }, fn sink(x: S) { print("sink") }, fn run() { sink(S { id: 5 }); print("end") } prints 'sink', 'end' and never 'close 5'. The same happens with a generic fn sink<T>(x: T). With fn sink<T>(x: ^T) and sink(^S { id: 5 }) it prints close 5. So a temporary with a Close impl bound to a read parameter is never closed after the call (a secret would not be scrubbed, a handle not released). Files: $JET_RUN_ROOT/Main/cv/g92b.jet, g92.jet. Acceptance: the temporary closes exactly once after the call on run and build; a golden example in Examples/features/memory proves it.

Folded #5821 "A task closure keeps its captured arguments alive after the body moves them out" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5989 (Map: Drop glue and moves: Close always runs,); 1 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Found by RustOut's Sglue slice (2026-10-23): with `task f(x)`, the closure environment keeps x alive for the task's whole life, so moving x out inside the body (or dropping it) frees nothing. In the compiler, ir_merge_runs(parts[at]) shared each IR part with its task, the merge rewrite then copy-on-write copied the functions (+0.24 GB at ir.build) and ir.opt copied them again (+0.55 GB); the x64 'free on a task' never freed anything before link. Workaround in the slice: pass tasks only keys and counts. Fix: a moved or last-use capture must transfer ownership out of the task environment (or the env must release a capture at its last use), same meaning on every tier (I9). Proof: an example whe

cards.title: Declared checks are enforced: DB effect rows, module-level #FX, comptime effects, lint deny, and SQL row-policy scope
cards.body: Found by Ballots-4 on dev 050dfbb4cd (probes $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/q/b4/sq/probe/s4, s5, s6). A function written `-[!DB.Write]>` that executes a write, and a package whose authority denies DB.Write, both check clean. DB effects of connection calls are not counted against written rows, so a written denial is a false promise (I1: the effect promise must be sound). The http_handler_captures example also checks clean under the handler ceiling -[Net, FS.Read]> while reaching the database.

Merged #6278 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: False E0740 (maximal effects) at comptime: xml.parse reaches XMLReader.next through trait dispatch. Body: Found by GoldC-2. `use core.encoding.xml as xml; fn f() -> Int { t :: xml.parse("<r/>") ?? panic("x"); 1 }; E :: comptime { f() }; fn run() { print(E) }` reports E0740 at Core/Encoding/Xml.jet:170 (XMLReader.next), only under comptime; run time is fine. The call graph goes StreamScanner.next -> Scanner.next (XmlEngine). Suspect: Effects/Checks.jet:1338-1361 resolves an unresolved trait dispatch to maximal effects, or :1037 an unresolved call, under the comptime check context. Blocks rustc_backed_aot_comptime_differentials variant2. I9: comptime must accept what run time accepts. Plan: Resolve trait-dispatch effects at comptime the same way as the run-time check (from the concrete impl or the trait row), not as maximal. Add the repro as a golden.

cards.title: Attach to a running program: the live inspector, span export and the dev console
cards.body:
Destination: a running Jet program can be attached to. `jet inspect live --attach PID` shows its task tree, channels, deadlines, effects, spans and allocations (D-OBSERVE-LIVE1=A, a viewer over the existing observability rails); spans export and replay with parent links; and the dev console attaches to the app's services, database resources and in-process router with read-only default authority, sandbox transactions and guards.

Why it matters: seeing a live program's state is the fastest way to find a stuck task or a bad request.

The tests/cases/live_inspect and event_observations rows in tests/known-failing.tsv belong to this card.

History: this card first collected every developer tool that did not build on the self-hosted toolchain (found by ToolsJet-2 while fixing #6346). On 2026-11-15 the other tools moved to their own cards: LSP #4917 and #6901-#6904, jet dev #5931, jet debug #6730, SemIndex #6630, flash #6905, embedding #6906, records #6907, Canvas #6618.

log.text: Every criterion is met (criteria blocked on other cards were moved there with their work); closed under the closest-first order (2026-11-16).

The behavior the deleted cases expected: tests/cases/authority/erased_devtools_publications_do_not_feed_panel_state.case: erased #Off devtools publications leave a DevPanel state field unpublished (two errors).

Nothing landed.

b71ca91930 (#6610): 9 tests/cases/web_dev/embedded_devserver_* rows fail because Core/Web/Devserver.jet has no DevServer.port or DevServer.serve (fixture apps hit E0102). They now fail in about 1 s and carry #6386 known-failing rows; building those two methods turns them green.

In the wave 30 cases run on dev bb770de593 + 6 patches, tests/cases/web_dev/embedded_devserver_rejects_hardlinked_source.case left its `jet dev app.jet` child running for 9.5 min. The testkit had no per-case deadline on it and stalled the whole suite until Main killed the child; the row then reads ERROR 'child terminated by signal'. Two defects: the devserver path never exits, and the testkit lacks a hard per-case wall deadline for dev/server children.

When JetLSP is ported, it reads JetCLISemIndex; JetSemIndex is folded into it or deleted, never wired as a second index (I8, Greenfield cutover).

cards.title: Core APIs that are not built yet: Bytes, Path.walk, timer channels, browser automation, config decode, Parquet/Arrow, Stream windows and the Vulkan provider
cards.body: Core APIs that the spec ratifies but the self-hosted runtime still answers with E2104 "not built yet". Their goldens and cases rows carry KNOWN-FAILING links here (owner ruling 2026-10-30). sys.decode (#5992), mod.load (#5993), service.tree and ws (#4957) keep their own cards. GoldC-3 owns Bytes.

log.text: Every criterion is met (criteria blocked on other cards were moved there with their work); closed under the closest-first order (2026-11-16).

Goal set to G3 only (was G1,G3). The two open rows, c7 (Parquet/Arrow reader beating pyarrow/polars) and c9 (Jet-runtime Vulkan provider), are Core completeness. They are not hand-off or durability, and they don't block a fresh clone from continuing work. The rows are unchanged.
Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match I9 tiers O0, O1, O2 and web (D-EXEC1, D-EXEC2=A: no interpreter or JIT).
HANDOFF 2026-11-06 (Main restart after the session crash): CoreCliLead takes over from Builder5: data_hostile guard, then the Severity E0772 collision, #6605, then this card.

c50 part A landed: 62a6e9f614 + 9730019b38 (GoldenRoots3). A runtime WebSocket hub (server connections join on upgrade and leave on drop; per-topic latest replayed on join; hub lock plus per-connection write lock) and the core.web.__live_publish row, route and registry entry; s1 and pack build OK. Main checked 62a6e9f614^..9730019b38: only the 12 part-A paths changed. Part B (the Web.jet publish call, docs, 2 expected outputs, new case db_scope_live_invalidation_reaches_ws_clients_and_reconnect_replays_latest) waits for the next seed rotation; with it the db_policy cases pass on o0-o2 except the pre-existing sqlite_blob row.

be271dbf74 (GoldenRoots3): root fix for the d77cf5ea53 Effect break. Registration/QualifiedTypes.jet canonicalizes imported bare type names in declared signatures, so a callee's imported type never resolves in the caller's scope. cards.title: UI cases where the Jet checker reports nothing: the error families the Rust checker emitted
cards.body:
Destination: every tests/ui row that expects an error gets it from JetSema. CoverPort's census of the wave-6 ui suite (2026-10-31) found 157 rows expecting an error the Jet checker never reports. Each is a missing sema check, not missing text. Two kinds:
1. An emit site exists but misses the case. The largest are Sema/Ownership/Checks.jet E0204 x10, E0121 x6, E2305 x5 and E0209 x4; Effects E3403 x6; Calls E0112 x5; Control E2402 x5; and Registration E3203 x5.
2. Whole families have no Jet emit site: E1293, E2806, E2807, E1402, the lint-policy E12xx codes, E0619, E0996, E0997 and others.

The census table (report5-nodiag.tsv) is under $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/CoverPort/out, which is not durable. Check it in first (c8), then prove c7 against the checked-in copy.

Lint checks moved to #6920 on 2026-11-15.

cards.title: The in-Jet SQL engine and core.auth leave Core for first-party `sql` and `auth` packages; core.db stays
cards.body:
Move card for #6150 (D-DB-AUTH-HOME1=A, ratified).

- Moves Core/Db/Sql.jet to a first-party `sql` battery and Core/Auth/Auth.jet to a first-party `auth` battery under Jetpack/Provider/Batteries/; both ship with Jet and `jet add sql` / `jet add auth` write the dependency line.
- core.db (connections, queries, rows, row policies, the SQLite driver) and `effect DB` stay in Core.
- The retired Core paths become registered errors naming `jet add` (what/why/fix and UI snapshots); `jet fix` rewrites imports.
- One greenfield cutover of every in-repo caller, example, golden and doc.

cards.title: core.metrics instruments and one deployable Service value (D-SERVICE-WORD1=A)
cards.body:
Destination: core.metrics declares counter, gauge and histogram instruments as constants exported through a provider, and one Service record (D-SERVICE-WORD1=A) feeds the dev runner and JetOS unit generation from one value, including a package's own built output.

Why it matters: services are described three times today (dev services D-DEV-SERVICES1, JetOS systemd units, infrastructure D-INFRA1), and Core has no metrics API (only Collections.Counter).

Done already: log levels are the typed LogLevel enum (dev ff909aea78, #6056 c2).

cards.title: Self-compile wall regressed from the best measured 9.62 s; get it back below, then keep improving
cards.body: Owner 2026-10-31: the best measured self-compile was 9.62 s. Track major regressions and fix them through the ongoing optimization work. History, from seed rotation s2/s3 builds of the compiler at the default level on a reserved slot: a0_019 (Oct 24) 11.3/9.4 s; a0_020 (Oct 28) 10.7/11.1 s; a0_021 22.6/16.8 s; a0_022 (Oct 30) 12.9/12.4 s; wave 17 chain s2 (Oct 31) 22.8 s. Today's dev compiler (wave 17 s2), fresh tree, 24 pinned CPUs, load 35-48: O0 19.9 s wall/56.5 user-s/6.6 GB; O1 (default) 54.7 s/91.9 user-s/6.9 GB; O2 175 s/143 user-s/5.3 GB, binary 83.4 MB (O1 69.0 MB). Wall far above user/cores means contention, so absolute numbers are inflated; the same-run interleaved A/B (a0_019 on its own source vs dev s2 on dev, 3 rounds, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/selfab) gives the real delta. Plan: bisect across seeds and waves with the stage store, attribute by phase (Tools/perf/budget trace), fix the roots as general compiler/runtime wins, and add a per-wave self-compile A/B against a pinned reference compiler so a regression over 5% is flagged in the wave REPORT.

This made the packages profile OOM at MemoryMax=24G. c11's proof set includes JetCli/Tests and Ssa.jet. The test pool fix (weighing each package by its measured peak) is with GoalsB-3.

Gauntlet-moving roots come first: c4 root F, c6 root B, c5 root C, c8, c11, c10. #6793 c2 S3 rekeys (about 1314 lookups, 70-90 slices, mostly hygiene) pause after the Scopes slice and resume after the gauntlet.

Level fact (Main, 2026-11-14, from G11Speed-5): `jet build` runs at O2 today. The optimize row's stock_build is "full" (JetFoundation/Source/Registry/BuildOptions.jet:48), and "full" is level 2 (Host.jet jet_cli_native_level); that agrees with I9. bb770de593's "default is O1" no longer holds. So the cold self-compile `jet build JetCli/run.jet` (ir.opt 13.5-15.7 s) is an O2 build, while the 9.62 s best was measured when the default was O1. Every A/B on this card names its level. c6's "default level" is O2, and root B is fixed by making each pass cheaper per function, never by dropping passes (the run-time peer floor is a hard gate).

Owner of the remaining load-reach work, 2026-11-12 01:3x: G4Ports-1, under #6759 c2. CoreReach.jet (steps 1-3, through 5d60ee4241) is module-granular: on seed-b10, hello plus x.abs() still loads 38 modules in 1043 ms, because Encoding Stream and Cbor reach core.math. The next step makes reach per declaration (lexer item runs as the unit, use targets loaded only when a reached run names the alias, conservative closure over impls and globally registered items, with the core_demand safety net kept), extending CoreReach.jet rather than adding a second mechanism. One SUB meets #6759 c2 and this card's c10.

Main, 2026-11-11: c10 step 3 is on dev as 5d60ee4241 (G8Scope-45 rev 3, landed as G5DevX-g8s45r). core.math loads by use, so sqrt1.jet checks 1364 functions instead of 1785, in 734 ms instead of 915. c10 is still open: it needs the per-phase breakdown on the batch compiler, each root fixed and proven on a second script, and the PortBars speed and memory pass. The cold-compile roots measured on the port twins (comptime.bodies, Core load, sema.finalize) are on #6759, whose c2 is the same load-by-reach rule.

c5: inspect_structure_text_and_json_expose_the_three_rows (G11Speed-4t) PASSes on seed-b8 (meet-reproof1), but it doesn't prove c5's acceptance, which is that every untraced build step of the c1 cell is traced and takes at most 2 s of wall. That needs a timed build trace. Not met.

c8 scope widened (Main, 2026-11-11): besides the layout-directory fsyncs, a cold build with seed-t23 waited 458 s in jbd2_log_wait_commit before its first span, because the build executor publishes its CAS blobs (put_blob -> publish_blob) and action records (put_record -> publish_action) durably, 15 puts about 25 s apart under a busy journal (Jetpack/Store/Source/Build/ArtifactStore.jet). The executor already reads a missing blob or bad record as a cache miss (Build/Cache.jet:239, :535), so G11Speed-7b makes those executor-only publishes non-durable (native-runtime and receipt publishes stay durable), with a miss-not-fault test, or skips them when caching is off. c8 is met by -7 plus -7b with the n=3 cold-store measurement.

criteria.text: Root F (proved by G11Speed's bisect, 2026-11-11, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G11Speed/report-bisect.md): 9afa7da76b (#6206 c22 CheckedText Hole/build) dropped the Distinct-only guard of sema_expression_checked_text_target, so every typed literal and Type.method() call walked every impl with string-cloning name lookups (77.9% of samples on seed-t22). criteria.text: A cold artifact store opens without per-directory fsync stalls, and the open is traced. Found by G11Speed on 2026-11-11 ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/G11Speed/b30/hang-finding.md): Jetpack/Store/Source/ArtifactStore/Store.jet (~964-971) creates the layout directories cas, ac, lto, locks, leases, quarantine, build-records and records through store_artifact_ensure_dir (Codec.jet:277), which fsyncs the parent after each mkdir. On a busy ext4 that cost 22.55 s across 8 fsyncs in one bench30k build (63 s total), all in an untraced gap between sema.finalize and ir.build; at 4G, 8 of 8 builds stalled. Fix: layout directories are recreated by any later run, so they aren't synced (per Codec.jet's own rule); durable records keep their sync; and a store.open trace span covers the work. Proof: a cold-store jet build of bench30k on the scratch disk ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT), n=3, shows store.open under 0.5 s in the trace and no untraced gap above 1 s, and the store crash-safety tests still pass.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #6966 c5, the card that owns this work (board cleanup).

criteria.text: Build reuse and the jet build binary store are off by default, per the standing caches-off order. Found by G11Speed on 2026-11-11: Executor.jet:324 restores any reusable step unconditionally, BuildExecute.jet:188 always opens the store when a build has steps, and Cli/BuildCache.jet:29 keeps the binary store on by default, with no switch (cli.md:504 documents made-or-reused). Fix (G11Speed-7c): a default build opens no store and puts nothing; opting in uses only an existing switch, or the executor API for tests if none exists, and any new public opt-in spelling goes to a ballot. cli.md and the BuildExecutor action-reuse test are updated in the same cutover. Proof: a test shows a default build opens no store; the opted-in reuse test passes; and cold and warm jet build Compiler are measured n=3 before and after.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #6966 c1: caches-off cutover gathered on one card

criteria.text: Cold script cost: `jet file.jet` for a script importing core.process compiles and runs from cold, with no reuse, in less wall time and peak memory than the original tool it replaces. Today (ScriptAPI-2, PortBars outputs, 2026-11-11) b4 pays 1.1-1.6 s and 355-388 MB per run, against originals of 37-1700 ms and 5.8-57 MB, so all 7 measured tool twins fail the speed and memory bars (e.g. census-snap2 21086 ms / 422 MB vs 1117 ms / 47.5 MB). Acceptance: a per-phase CPU and peak-RSS breakdown of that script on the batch compiler names each root (parse/import/sema/lowering/emit/link of Core modules the script does not reach, eager whole-module work, arena sizing); each root is fixed in the general path and proven on a second script; the PortBars speed and memory bars pass on the census-snap2 and roots-mjs entries with cold compile counted. Reuse is not the fix: the standing order counts cold compile time. Proof: `jet Tools/gauntlet/PortBars.jet` speed and memory bars for census-snap2 and roots-mjs, cold compile counted.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #6759 c21, the card that owns this work (board cleanup).

criteria.text: Checking a root never needs gigabytes. With seed-b6 at d97d742871 and MemoryMax=6G, `jet check` was OOM-killed on 8 roots: Compiler/JetBackend/Tests, Compiler/JetCli, Compiler/JetCli/Commands, Compiler/JetCli/Commands/Tests, Compiler/JetCli/Tests, its GateProjection.fixture and RustForeign.fixture, and Compiler/JetDriver/Tests. Other scopes peaked at 6.0-6.8 GB. A collect-all census records the peak RSS of `jet check` for every in-repo root, and each phase's memory owner (parse, register, comptime, sema, IR) is named from a profile of the worst root. Every root's peak is then at most 3 GB, with no caching or reuse. Proof: a committed collect-all census of `jet check` peak RSS for every in-repo root, every row at or under 3 GB.

cards.title: Canvas runs on the self-hosted toolchain: its scenarios restored, parser spans, the shared Core-call record and one edit-transaction seam
cards.body:
Destination: `jet dev --canvas` (Compiler/JetDevserver/Source/Canvas) runs on the self-hosted toolchain on solid foundations. The 88 browser scenarios deleted in the #6035 c3 cutover are back. Functions and spans come from the parser, Core names come from the shared Core-call record, and every edit crosses one transaction seam. Plain `jet dev` stays terminal-first (D-CANVAS-CMD1=A). Scenario proof (used here and on the Canvas cards): `jet run --allow=Env,Exec,FS,IO,Net,Time Tools/canvas-test/Run.jet -- scenario --scenario --port

`, run against a running `jet dev --canvas`, prints PASS. The Canvas product moved out of #6418 and #6419 by owner ruling 2026-11-06. It runs inside JetDevserver, so it waits on #5931. cards.title: Reactive notebook: `jet notebook` reruns only affected cells, with typed controls, reconnect, attached outputs and diff-friendly .jetnb files
cards.body:
Destination: `jet notebook` runs a reactive kernel. Editing a cell reruns its pure descendants and marks effectful ones for confirmation (D-DX-CELLS1=A). Typed function arguments render as controls. A browser reconnects only with matching identity and authority. Outputs stay attached to their cells. A `.jetnb` file holds only source, so `git diff` shows one cell's change. The notebook runs and builds like a program, and a Jupyter kernel adapter exists.

The notebook rows in tests/known-failing.tsv are on #6418 (unbuilt `jet notebook`, E2104).

Moved out of #6418 by owner ruling 2026-11-06. The notebook app moved to #6922 on 2026-11-15.

log.text: Every criterion is met (criteria blocked on other cards were moved there with their work); closed under the closest-first order (2026-11-16).
Cleaned 2026-11-15. The notebook app (c11-c14) went to #6922. c10 (the D-DX-CELLS1 proof stub) merged into c1.

criteria.text: Editing a defining cell reruns only its pure transitive dependents automatically, records the dependency order, and marks effectful dependents for confirmation, labeling skipped work stale (D-DX-CELLS1=A).
criteria.evidence: Moved to #6922 c5, the card that owns this work (board cleanup).

criteria.text: A typed function argument renders as a validated control, and changing the control reruns the affected cells, while invalid input keeps an explicit error state.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #6922 c6, the card that owns this work (board cleanup).

criteria.text: Deleting a defining cell scrubs its bindings and invalidates the dependent outputs, and an old cached value is never shown as current.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #6922 c7, the card that owns this work (board cleanup).

criteria.text: Closing and reopening the browser reconnects to the same bounded kernel only when the source and build identity and the authority checks pass, and an unauthorized reconnect is rejected with a registered error.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #6922 c8, the card that owns this work (board cleanup).

criteria.text: Text, HTML, SVG and table results stay attached to their cell, imported output stays quarantined, and exports report any semantics they drop.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #6922 c9, the card that owns this work (board cleanup).

criteria.text: A `.jetnb` file holds only source and cell markers; outputs are recomputed when the notebook runs and are not stored between runs, and editing one cell changes only that cell's lines in `git diff`. Proof: a tests/cases notebook row under `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter jetnb`.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #6922 c10, the card that owns this work (board cleanup).

criteria.text: A Jupyter kernel adapter runs Jet cells: a scripted `jupyter nbconvert --execute` of a three-cell notebook passes where Jupyter is installed and is SKIP-HOST with a reason elsewhere.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #6922 c11, the card that owns this work (board cleanup).

criteria.text: `jet run nb.jetnb` and `jet build nb.jetnb` print the same output as running every cell in order, and a corpus of 20 notebooks reruns from a clean state with identical output 20 of 20 times. For comparison, 4% of Jupyter notebooks reproduce, and marimo cannot build a native binary. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter notebook/run_and_build_match_cell_order` and `--filter notebook/corpus_reruns_identically`.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #6922 c12, the card that owns this work (board cleanup).

criteria.text: Editing one cell of a 10-cell notebook reruns only its dependents and shows the new output sooner than marimo does on the equivalent notebook (Jet time over marimo time below 1.00). Proof: a committed measurement under Docs/audits with both timings and the commands.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #6922 c13, the card that owns this work (board cleanup).

criteria.text: (was #4272) {"decisionId": "D-DX-CELLS1", "text": "Rerun pure descendants automatically and mark effectful work for confirmation; Gains: Only affected cells rerun.; Deleted bindings are scrubbed.; Stale output is always labeled.. Losses: A live kernel keeps bounded state..", "proof": {"kind": "required Jet production integration #Test and reviewed golden/receipt", "testName": "d_dx_cells1_contract", "suite": "tests/ratified/P08.jet (proposed Jet-side suite, not an existing/passing fixture)", "golden": "tests/ratified/expected/P08/d_dx_cells1.out (proposed; external-state or measurement cases also attach source-bound receipt)", "requiredCases": ["edit pure ancestor reruns only pure descendants; effectful cells require confirmation; delete binding scrubs it; stale output labeled; bounded retained kernel state", "one resident game source/runtime session with identical headless/rendered events and authoritative Canvas routes", "typed local SQL interactive and CI command with plans/limits; optional browser projection; remote engine requires explicit provider authority", "local app selection shares reload/reconnect and serves real requests; local-only default; close shuts down resident process"]}} (was #4275 c77)
criteria.evidence: Merged into #6619 c1: D-DX-CELLS1=A's required cases (pure descendants rerun, effectful confirmation, deleted bindings scrubbed, stale output labeled) are c1 and c3

criteria.text: `jet notebook --app` starts a loopback server that renders the notebook's cell outputs, layouts and controls from the running notebook kernel, with no second evaluator.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #6922 c1: the notebook app has its own card

criteria.text: Two browser tabs on one notebook app get separate typed session state, run callbacks in a fixed order, and reset or reconnect independently; one tab cannot read or change the other's state.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #6922 c2: the notebook app has its own card

criteria.text: Editing the notebook or one of its typed functions under `jet dev` updates the running app, keeps state whose type did not change, and names the reason when it resets state or shows a stale output.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #6922 c3: the notebook app has its own card

criteria.text: The notebook app binds to loopback only unless sharing is asked for, and prints a machine-readable receipt of its bind address, sharing, data it reads and trust grants.

cards.body:
Destination: jet_semindex (called by jet_cli) has every behavior that only the deleted, never-compiled jet_semindex drafts described. Those drafts are in Compiler/JetSemIndex/Source/ at 76cbe208be. They cover type dossiers, structural audit, package facts, overlays, the query API, the LSP symbol database, semantic blame, native doc paths, and search by effect or by example.

The tests/cases/semindex rows in tests/known-failing.tsv belong to this card.

cards.title: Compiler/build.jet declares the whole project: every artifact, generated table, toolchain, chain stage and profile is one build graph
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-11-07: make full use of Jet's customizable build function for this project; card it, do not build it now.

Today Compiler/build.jet declares one target, the jet executable. Everything else is assembled outside the build graph, each piece in its own serial step: the self-host chain (Tools/agent/chain/chain.sh), the runtime pack (cc-pack and pack, with musl found through JET_PACK_MUSL_LIB), the Jetpack engine (Jetpack/Bootstrap/Assemble.jet, then a separate jet build inside the packages suite: 3 min quiet, 13 min under load), the generated registry tables (regenerated by hand and checked at precommit; a stale CoreEnumRows failed a landing on 2026-11-07), and the test and release tools.

The Build API already offers add_executable, add_library, add_test, add_package, add_publish, add_install, add_doc, action, generate, toolchain, probe, signing and embed, the registered build options, and core.build graph receipts with receipt_diff.

log.text: Every criterion is met (criteria blocked on other cards were moved there with their work); closed under the closest-first order (2026-11-16).

SpeedLead: build.jet cannot list a folder at plan time (b.find returns files only, walks into .jet, and is not recorded as a plan input; #4833 known-failing). So c6 keeps STAGE_FOLDERS and STAGE_FILES as a kernel.tsv row, plus a tests/guards check that every top-level entry of a split stage package (except Generated and dot entries) is listed, so the list cannot go stale silently. The .jet/deps alias hole touches 5 to 6 files in two packages and is now its own criterion; c6 does not depend on it.

c6 layout ruling (Main): the build-graph contract stays. SpeedLead moves the 4 kept generated sources into <pkg>/Generated/ (JetFoundation PreludeMarkers, JetSema PreludeDerives and PreludeUnits, JetLexer KeywordSpans). Stages read those packages top-level entries minus Generated/, derived at plan time, not a hand list, plus the kept files through .reads. The rejected alternative (narrow folders plus about 105 explicit files) would be a stale-prone closed list. Owner Q20 is withdrawn. Validator defect found by SpeedLead: both validators compare spelled folder paths, so a dependency bound at .jet/deps on the same real folder escapes the rule. It is fixed in the same patch by comparing resolved folders, with a #Test.

c6 blocker (SpeedLead): the self-host stages read the 17 Compiler folders whole, and the build-graph rule (Graph.jet:109-121, Jetpack Validation.jet:173-177, spec.md:5050, E3502) refuses step outputs inside them: the runtime step outputs under JetCli/.jet/build, and the c5 kept outputs (Prelude copies, KeywordSpans.jet). Main ruling: an output under a .jet or .git part being outside the folder read is a defect fix (one meaning with the folder snapshot, Cache.jet build_folder_skipped). SpeedLead lands it with a BuildGraphRules #Test. Allowing an output inside a read folder when the reader also reads it changes the spec contract, so it is owner Q20. SpeedLead is costing the keep-the-rule alternative.

c4 landed on dev as 42d3bedfe8 (SpeedLead lane-commit; precommit census on a0_039: check, build, runtime from jet build Compiler, self-check, Core self-check). It is the owner (A) stopgap shape (host cc plus musl), removed under #6687. On master as merge cb5a55054d, the exact tested dev tree. A cherry-pick conflicted in the generated Docs/spec/safety.md and would have given master an unbuilt tree, so the merge also carries 1f8f46177e (#6690) and 775f3b07ae (#6686). Main updated its precommit census for trees where jet build Compiler writes the pack. c5 (generated tables as kept build outputs) is next, and c6 (s2 and s3 as build actions) is approved.

Owner ruling 2026-11-08 on commit 4: "A as stopgap but removed when we have 100% jet." So c4 lands in the (A) shape: a fresh clone builds with the dev shell or a host cc plus static musl, and ReuseSeedRuntime.jet is deleted. The host C requirement goes when #6687 (no C dependency) closes; the fresh-clone criterion there proves it. Landing waits for a0_039 to be the current seed, because a0_038 rejects the new build.jet (Build.folder arity). SpeedLead holds the tested patch (LaneCheck CHECK OK on dev c884e9421c).

Commit 4 is held for an owner question (2026-11-08). Under c4, `jet build Compiler` builds the runtime pack, so it needs cc plus a static musl libc.a. A fresh clone with neither stops at the probes, so bootstrap.md "From a fresh clone: no Nix" (seed build plus ReuseSeedRuntime) stops being true. Using the toolchain own jet cc inside build steps needs new public build API: steps run sandboxed (bwrap, cleared env, no net) and see only the builder folder and probe results, not the Hangar cc pack. The pack also lacks nm (RuntimePack symbol gate) and ships compiler-rt instead of libgcc.a/libgcc_eh.a. Options for the owner: (A) the fresh clone uses the dev shell or a host cc plus musl; (B) a ballot for a jet-cc build-step surface; (C) keep ReuseSeedRuntime as an exception. SpeedLead finishes the rest of c4 as a tested patch meanwhile.

Main ruling, commit 4: `.file(b.found(p))` accepts a find_program result too (it already accepts find_folder), within the approved D-BUILD-GRAPH1/D-BUILD-TREES1 surface, so no ballot. The found program gets the same sandbox visibility it gets as a step tool; the action key covers its bytes and its probe fact; the old refusal and its snapshot go; a cc case proves it. The runtime pack logic moves to Compiler/Toolchain/RuntimePack.jet, run as one b.run step. Also fixed: staged inputs lost the exec bit.

Commit 3 landed as 74bbf2a07c (the find_folder probe, with no caller; E3505 with a UI snapshot). Main decided commit 4: flatten jet-runtime/ to fixed paths, with the identity in native.key. It is an internal pack format, one cutover across the CLI lookup, ReuseSeedRuntime, the chain store, the pack cache and publishing, with no fallback reader; the alternative was a new public step.output_folder API (I8). The vendored C is reached through source-less foreign packages at Core/Vendor/Sqlite3 and Core/Vendor/Mbedtls (not a Core/package.jet, which would mark Core as its own project); this needs a side-effect census first. A flake.nix LIBRARY_PATH export is allowed only with a host glibc-link proof.

Owner ruling 2026-11-08 (asked via Main): Compiler/build.jet builds jet with Core embedded, the committed generated tables (D-BUILD-ROWS1 = A, kept: true) and the runtime pack (jet-runtime: Core/Vendor C compiled with cc, static musl linked) as one complete toolchain. Tools, the docs site and Jetpack stay out of it. Folder inputs (D-BUILD-TREES1 option A: b.folder / b.dependency(name).folder / find_folder, hashed per file) are approved for the trees this needs (Core/, Core/Vendor, Compiler/JetRuntime). The cc and musl needs end with #6328 c11 and Jet-native db/TLS. Owner: SpeedLead (already owns Compiler/build.jet); top priority, ahead of #6328.

Owner ruling 2026-11-08 (asked via Main): D-BUILD-ROWS1 = A. Generated tables stay in git as build outputs (.output(path, kept: true)): jet build Compiler rewrites them when inputs change and refuses hand edits; the precommit freshness check becomes build plus clean tree. D-BUILD-TREES1: owner accepts folder inputs but rejects the scope as drafted: Tools are separate from the compiler build (Compiler/build.jet covers the compiler and Core, not Tools), and questions why the compiler build needs C sources, cc and musl at all. Scope question pending. Blocker (1) is cleared: a0_037 (3a8dd83e79) contains every D-BUILD-GRAPH1 step (4361eec2f4 is an ancestor).

Main 2026-11-08 02:00, BuildLead final handoff (slot ended). Landed: C4 profiles 3af734e9cb; step 1 b.run/b.found/action_timeout ccf9915f44; b.action and b.legacy retired 74942e812c; step 2 b.host/b.jet/one parallel graph c9c3ce97a6; gate fix 8a85d45051 (a b.jet() step gets the running compiler's identity); step 4 receipts, times and jet inspect build --times 64f57f1583; step 5 b.dependency(name).file(path) 509708b651; step 6 b.image(target) a749167d57; step 7 a step never overwrites a file no build made 4361eec2f4; closed-list kernel rows ec519cce83. Criteria per BuildLead: 6 and 7 met in code (Main meets them after the c65 run #3 proof); 1 partly met (the graph and the jet target; other targets need D-BUILD-TREES1); 2 blocked by D-BUILD-ROWS1 (every generator writes committed files a step may not overwrite; CoreSourceRows also writes outside Compiler/); 3 and 4 blocked by D-BUILD-TREES1 (jet embeds all of Core/, PrebuildRuntime.jet is in Tools/, and no probe finds a folder); 5 blocked by #6623. Owner ballots drafted, not yet adversarially reviewed, in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/BuildLead/ballots/. D-BUILD-ROWS1 recommends kept outputs: .output(path, kept: true) rewrites a committed table when its inputs change and refuses hand edits; the alternatives are build-only files or today's hand-run generators. D-BUILD-TREES1 recommends folder inputs (b.dependency(name).folder(path), b.folder(path)) plus a find_folder probe; the alternatives are listing a dependency's files one by one, or keeping the scripts. Both pass Validate.jet apart from draft:true and an empty reviewPasses. No scripts were deleted.

Main 2026-11-07 23:50: BuildLead reports the D-BUILD-GRAPH1 API done locally (steps 1-2 on dev; 4 records, 5 dependency, 6 image and 7 refuse-overwrite landing in order). Three blockers stop migrating Compiler/build.jet. (1) build.jet is compiled by the seed, so it needs a seed with steps 1-7; Main cuts a0_038 after they land. (2) Owner question: refuse-overwrite means the generated row files (CoreCallRows and so on) leave git and come from jet build Compiler, so jet check or jet test on a fresh member fails until a build runs. Choose untracked generated rows or keep the committed rows with their precommit freshness check. (3) Owner question: C2/C3/C5 read trees outside Compiler/ (Core, the runtime C sources, Tools) and need cc and musl. That needs folder inputs or listing a dependency's files, which is new API and needs a ballot. Ballot drafts for (2) and (3) go to $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/BuildLead/ballots/; they have no adversarial review yet.

cards.title: jet debug's contract on the self-hosted toolchain: the DAP wire, honest session states, accepted revisions and one watch parser
cards.body:
Destination: `jet debug` keeps a Jet-level contract on the self-hosted toolchain. `--break` and `--dap` drive one session. Attach, pause, restart and raw frames work over the production DAP wire, or are refused with E2236. Every end state is honest. Breakpoints and values refer to the accepted revision, and inspection never changes the guest. Watches parse with the compiler's parser. DAP has conditional breakpoints, logpoints and evaluate, and its speed is measured against lldb.

The tests/cases/debug/dap_cli_* rows in tests/known-failing.tsv belong to this card.

Related cards (2026-11-15 split): debug info and values #6918, record and replay #6919.

cards.title: A string or byte literal body after an effect row lexes as a typed head, so escapes and holes are wrong
cards.body: Found by G12Docs-4 (G12Docs-69) on seed-b13: h: fn() -[]> String { "a\nb" } prints a literal backslash-n. Compiler/JetLexer/Source/Lexer/Payload.jet string_head_modes reads Ident { followed by a string as a typed head (raw text, holes, undecoded escapes), and its only exemption for a return type, returned_type_at, recognizes just ) -> before the type. After an effect arrow -[E]> the body String { ... } becomes the typed head String{...}: \n stays raw, \u{41} becomes \u plus a hole, and interpolation breaks. The [U8] { byte head has the same gap. char literals, return, parenthesized and if bodies are unaffected. It is wrong output with no diagnostic.

log.text: Both criteria met: the literal-body case (c1) and the parser-owned typed-head decision with an unchanged golden corpus (c2, p237 dev ab95db25f2).

criteria.text: A function body that is a string, byte or interpolated literal lexes as a body after every return-type form: -> T, an effect arrow -[E]> T with one or several effects, generic, list, map, optional, fallible and qualified return types. Its escapes decode and its holes interpolate exactly as in the same body after -> T. A case covers each literal kind (escapes, \u{...}, interpolation, byte strings) with and without an effect row, at O0, O1 and O2, and a real typed head written as a body expression still lexes as a typed head.
criteria.evidence: dev 6a10ad7d0c, gate-p64 jet, b53proofs 2026-11-14 (dev 99aa698189): jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter language_features/literal_body_reads_as_a_body_after_every_return_type_form -> PASS 1/FAIL 0 (each literal kind with and without an effect row, O0/O1/O2, and a typed head).

criteria.text: The typed-head decision is made in one place from the parser's knowledge of the return-type position, not from a lexer token-pattern guess that each new return-type spelling must extend. The tests/ and Examples corpus show no output change other than the fixed cases, by the golden profile at O0, O1 and O2. Proof: `jet test Compiler --profile golden` on O0, O1 and O2 changes only the fixed cases, and `git grep -n returned_type_at -- Compiler/JetLexer` prints nothing.
criteria.evidence: dev ab95db25f2 (lexer heuristic removed by 5c858f4290): `git grep -n returned_type_at -- Compiler/JetLexer` prints nothing; p237 batch compiler full golden profile PASS 5026, FAIL 0 on o0, o1 and o2, with 0 new failures against p236.

cards.title: A runtime stop names the same source site on every tier: web images carry the location table native images use
cards.body: Since ae7fe7adaf, a stop raised inside Core names the user's call that reached Core, read from the image's location table (.debug_jetline). A web image has no such table, so it prints the Core site instead; the spec allows that fallback for an image with no location table. That makes one program report different stop sites on native and web, which breaks I9's one meaning across tiers. Found by SweepFix-162 (web-no-exec, 2026-11-15): the web host had also answered mprotect(PROT_EXEC) with success, so the frame walk trapped. That trap is fixed, and the e1003 web case now pins the two sites separately instead of comparing bytes.

log.text: Met on p237: web stop reports match native user-line reports byte for byte.

criteria.text: A stop raised inside Core reports the user's call site (file and line) on web exactly as on native: the web image carries the location table (or its equivalent), and the stop report reads it. Proof: the e1003 case and the golden stops IntPowNegativeStop, FloatBitsRangeStop and TypedAbsI64Min compare their web output byte for byte with native's user-line report.
criteria.evidence: p237 batch compiler (dev ab95db25f2; case landed in ba783d11b9 lineage): cases FailureTierParity/core_stops_name_the_users_call_on_web_as_on_native PASS (jet build --target web of IntPowNegativeStop, FloatBitsRangeStop and TypedAbsI64Min, compared byte for byte with the native goldens .out/.err.out) and runtime_e1003_web_uses_the_same_stop_metadata_and_exit_70 PASS; the three goldens PASS on o0, o1 and o2.

cards.title: Publish the Jet trust root at a stable address so signatures have an anchor
cards.body:
Owner acquired `jet-lang.dev` 2026-08-25. This card makes signing possible later without doing the key ceremony now.

WHY THIS IS THE FIRST DOMAIN CARD: card #2157 deferred official signed publication partly because there was nowhere to publish. A signature is only worth something if a verifier can independently obtain the public key from a place the project controls. Owning a domain supplies that place.

MEASURED TODAY: the only working catalog is signed by a hardcoded test key `jet-test-index-v1` whose seed is 32 bytes of the value 7 (`target-nixfeed/sign-test.mjs`). Anyone can forge it. Card #2157 requires deleting it rather than promoting it.

WHAT TO BUILD: a documented, stable location under the owned domain that serves the Jet public signing key or keys, in a form the client already understands (`trust/nix-index-v1.ed25519.pub` is the current shape read by `IndexClient::from_roots_with_mode` in `crates/jetpack/src/NixIndex.rs`). Include key id, algorithm and validity, and a documented rotation story even if rotation is manual at first.

EXPLICITLY NOT THIS CARD: generating production key material, choosing custody, or signing a real catalog. Those stay owner-gated on #2157. This card only establishes the address and the format so the later ceremony has somewhere to land.

TRAP: fetching a key over HTTPS is not the same as trusting it. The client must pin or verify the key it already has rather than accepting whatever the host returns. A trust root served over a network is only an anchor if the client refuses substitutions.

cards.title: Task outcomes: domain errors reach the joiner, checked failures stay inside the task, and core.tasks has no silent rail
cards.body:
Destination: a task's domain error reaches its joiner as that error, a checked failure inside a task becomes `TaskFailure.Panicked` for the joiner instead of stopping the process, Core declares the one `TaskFailure` enum sema and the runtime share, core.tasks has no sentinel values or silent drops, sending on a closed channel fails with SendError (D-SEND-ERROR1=A), and blocking task functions declare `Time.Wait`.

Why: a domain error reported as a panic, or a failure that vanishes, makes concurrent code impossible to reason about.

Source: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f012, with merged cards #1302, #3180, #3240, #3443, #3900, #3989, #4116 and #5468. Channels and streams went to #6926, cancellation and supervision to #6927, atomics to #6928, callback failures to #6929, and the release, view-trap and replay contracts to #5989, #4620 and #6012.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Prove task outcomes and structured cancellation (groups, all/race/any, timers/select, sibling drain, cooperative wait cancellation) with explicit task-failure versus domain-failure identity. Reconcile the two `TaskFailure` meanings into one owner, and stop ordinary `Err` from being flattened into a panic.

## Current state
- There are two meanings. Core has `pub struct TaskFailure { message: String, raised: Bool }` (`Core/tasks/tasks.jet:35-38`). The host and sema use an enum: `JetTaskFailure::{Cancelled, DeadlineBlown, Panicked(String)}` (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/TaskGroup.rs:40-83`) and `Type.Result(ok, Type.Named("TaskFailure"))` (`Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/TaskGroups.jet:339-341`). `TaskFailure` is a registered error leaf in `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/FailureLaw.jet:22`.
- Err flattening: `jet_task_flatten_result` maps an ordinary body `Err(e)` to `jet_task_failure_from_code("TASK_BODY_FAILED", …)`, which falls through to `Panicked(reason)` (TaskGroup.rs:44, :52-62). A domain error is therefore reported as a panic, which violates criterion 3 and the research warning.
- Witnesses with goldens: `Examples/features/concurrency/{task_group,task_all,all_failfast(.err),select_channel,completion_order,release_join_failure,race_cancel,cancel_cleanup,task_panic(.err)}.jet`. The race_cancel and cancel_cleanup goldens now exist.
- The finding is at `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f012`.

## Changes
1. One owner: make `Core/tasks/tasks.jet` declare `TaskFailure` as the enum `Cancelled | DeadlineBlown | Panicked(message: String)` that sema and host already use, and delete the `{message, raised}` struct and `exception()`. Migrate callers.
2. Domain errors: a task body typed `T E!` joins to `(E | TaskFailure)!`, so the domain `E` stays itself and is not rewrapped. Change `jet_task_flatten_result(s)` and the JIT and interpreter equivalents to propagate `E`. Add sema typing for the joined union in `TaskGroups.jet`.
3. Add `Examples/features/concurrency/task_domain_error.jet` with a golden. A group child returns `Err(ParseError…)`; the parent matches it as `ParseError`, not `Panicked`; siblings are drained, which is observed through a cleanup print.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=concurrency/ Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `for f in task_group task_all select_channel completion_order release_join_failure race_cancel cancel_cleanup task_domain_error; do Tools/agent/jet-env jet run Examples/features/concurrency/$f.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/concurrency/$f.out; done` gives empty diffs, and the same holds with `--interpret`.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test task_control_tiers` and `--test taskgroup_parameter_tiers` pass.

## Batch
batch-core-tasks: the tasks family Core source, sema and host flatten, retested with the concurrency goldens.

## Dependencies
None.

criteria.text: D-SEND-ERROR1=A is built (ratified 2026-11-13). sender.send(v) returns nothing on success and fails with SendError<T> when no receiver remains; err.value moves the unsent value back. Core declares conversions from SendError and Closed into Err, and from SendError into Closed, so a bare send in run, a task block or a function naming no error type passes the failure up with a message naming the send, and inside a function failing with Closed it passes up as Closed. Freeing queued values runs each value's drop. Depends on #6787 (generic conversions into Err). Proof: cases for a bare send, send ?? handler recovering err.value, and a send inside a Closed function, on O0, O1 and O2; every in-repo send caller is migrated in the same cutover.
criteria.evidence: Moved to #6926 c21, the card that owns this work (board cleanup).

questions.text: what is the best theoretical greenfield solution?
questions.answer: The best design is the posted B, improved, now listed as A: send fails with SendError, and err.value hands the unsent value back. The cost the posted ballot charged it, 282 lines to edit, goes away once Core declares that SendError converts into the general Err and into Closed. With that, a bare send in run, a task block or a plain function simply passes its failure up, and a probe shows that pattern working with a stand-in error. So no value is ever lost silently, a program that cares gets the value back, and send agrees with the already ratified try_send. Two things remain and are named: sends inside functions that promise never to fail need ??, and values still queued when the last receiver is dropped are freed, as in Rust, Go and Kotlin; freeing runs each value's drop, so what it holds is released. The build must also teach error conversions to apply to generic errors, which the seed does not do yet.

cards.title: Unicode text and regex: full case folding, positions, display widths, producers and regex literal fixes
cards.body:
Destination: core.text handles all of Unicode the same on every tier: full case mapping and folding, normalization, distinct byte, scalar and grapheme positions, display widths, honest producers, text built from whole UTF-8 runs, one name per case operation, and regex accessors and literals that teach the working form.

Why it matters: Latin-1-only case folding and byte-at-a-time text are silent wrong answers for most of the world's text.

State (dev 168e1e9e92): Core/Text/Runtime/KernelUnicodeString.jet holds lower, upper and casefold; Core/Text/String.jet has both lower and to_lower; Core/Regex/Regex.jet is a bounded backtracking NFA over UTF-8 bytes.

Decisions: D-UNICODE-CASE1=A, D-TEXT-CONTROL1=A, D-CHAR-SCALAR1=A, D-CORE-ONE-NAME1=A.

Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md (finding core-f038).

Moved out 2026-11-15: number formatting, templates, locales and diffs to the text formatting card; message catalogs to the i18n card; the build-time regex literal to #6476; checked text sinks to #6852.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Close the core.text/core.regex/codec contract on scalar boundaries, case and normalization, regex complexity and invalid encoding, with exercised witnesses. Fix the one real gap: case folding beyond Latin-1.

**Current state**
- Core/text/text.jet:14-19: UTF-8 decode, Hangul NFD/NFC, UAX #29 graphemes and words, and width are Jet. Case mapping is Latin-1 only, and full case-fold tables map to identity. :73-78 `lower`/`upper`/`casefold` → `map_case` (:467). `casefold` is just `lower`, so `casefold("Straße")` stays `straße`.
- :82-88 `nfc`/`nfd`/`nfkc`/`nfkd`/`graphemes`/`words` exist.
- Core/regex/regex.jet:15-18 is a bounded backtracking NFA over UTF-8 bytes with ASCII-only `ignore_case`. :488-498 `budget_limit` is (nodes+1)×(min(bytes,4096)+1)×32, clamped to [4096, 1,000,000]. :458-461 caps quantifiers at 4096.
- Examples/features/text/unicode_text.jet, unicode_17.jet and regex.jet have goldens. Related open cards: #1471 (regex gaps, building), #3370 (producers), #3107 (index boundaries).

**Changes**
1. Core/text/text.jet: generate full Unicode simple and full case mapping plus C+F folding tables into Jet data, the same way the existing normalization tables are generated. Route `map_case` and `casefold` through them. Casefold is locale-neutral; Turkish dotted I is not special-cased. Update the header comment at :14-19.
2. Regex: keep the byte NFA and budget. Document in regex.jet that budget exhaustion is a typed failure, and add a witness that proves it. `ignore_case` stays ASCII, stated explicitly; Unicode case-insensitive regex belongs to #1471.
3. Invalid encoding: `String.from_bytes` → None and codec `EncodingError` are the policy. Add a witness for lossy vs strict where core.text exposes it.
4. Add Examples/features/text/unicode_contracts.jet plus its golden. Record unsupported cells as printed lines.
5. Owned vs view costs: measure only the rows exercised above, through the existing text perf cell. Make no claim without a receipt.

**Proof**
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden text/unicode_contracts`: passes.
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden text/unicode_text` and `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=text/regex …`: still pass. Existing goldens change only where casefold output was wrong.
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden text/unicode_contracts` passes on O0, O1 and O2.

**Batch**
batch-core-text: Core/text and Core/regex Jet only, proved by text goldens.

**Dependencies**
None. New parser or control APIs (for example, a Unicode regex mode) need their own ballot (criterion 3).

cards.title: JSON beyond decode: JMESPath queries, merge patch, diff, update, JSONC, field selection and exclusion
cards.body:
Destination: Core's JSON goes past parse and decode with strict, bounded, typed operations: standard JMESPath queries, RFC 7386 merge patch, diff and update, an explicit JSONC dialect, and runtime field selection and exclusion that never weaken validation or emit hidden fields.

Why it matters: these are the everyday JSON jobs of config tools and services; each done ad hoc loses validation or data.

Decisions: D-CORE-JMESPATH1=A (bounded standard JMESPath at core.data.jmespath), D-ENC-DYN1=A (typed decode stays strict).

Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md (findings core-f055, core-f058).

Moved out 2026-11-15: other formats to the data formats card; MIME to #6874; HTTP client to #3665; routes to #6864; WebSocket to #6878; Codable to #3236; reactive UI examples to #6552.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Record what full versus selective JSON decoding actually does: validation scope, failure timing, and repeated scans and allocations. Ordinary decode must never silently weaken validation, and any lazy expert API goes to a ballot.

## Current state
- Core/encoding/json.jet:93-95: `reader(text)` is a pull parser whose first call validates and materializes the whole value, after which it walks events. There is no demanded-prefix extraction.
- The shipped bounded event reader is the host `jet_enc_json_reader(input: FileReader, limits)` (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/EncodingStream.rs:534; dispatcher crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core.jet:749), with a golden at Examples/features/serde/encoding_json_stream.jet.
- Typed `json.decode<T>` is compiler lowering through `jet_std_json_decode_lenient` (Core.jet:731).
- Examples/features/serde/shape_projection.jet depends on argv, the environment and a DB (:6, :30-31, :35), so it cannot be a golden. It is a Shape-projection witness, not a selective-decoding one.

## Changes
1. New Examples/features/serde/json_selective.jet with its .out. It runs one document through three paths: (a) `json.parse` in full, (b) `json.decode<Small>` projecting 1 of 20 fields, and (c) `json.reader(^file)` events, stopping after the first key. The inputs are: valid; malformed inside a skipped subtree; trailing garbage after the root; a duplicate key in a skipped subtree; and an invalid UTF-8 escape in a skipped string. It prints, for each path, whether and where it fails.
2. Expected law: (a) and (b) validate the whole document and fail identically. (c) fails when it reaches the bad bytes, or at `finish`, and the failure timing is printed. If (b) accepts malformed skipped data or trailing garbage, fix the lenient typed decoder at its owner so that typed decode stays strict (D-ENC-DYN1).
3. Measurement: `Tools/agent/jet-env jet perf run` on a scratch program over a 1 MB document records wall time and allocations for (a), (b) and (c), plus repeated `parse` calls, and the numbers go on the card.
4. Record the cell `demanded-prefix or lazy extraction: unsupported`. Any expert lazy or borrowed API is a ballot (criterion 4), not a change to ordinary decode.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/json_selective cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run --interpret Examples/features/serde/json_selective.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/serde/json_selective.out` prints nothing.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/encoding_json_stream cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` still passes.

## Batch
batch-core-encoding: a JSON witness plus at most one decoder fix.

## Dependencies
None.

criteria.evidence: dev aeeb2c479c (GoldenRoots3): new golden serde/json_selective passes on o0/o1/o2. One 20-field document goes through parse, decode<Small> (1 of 20 fields) and the reader, valid and with a malformed skipped field, trailing garbage, a second root, a duplicate key or bad escape inside a skipped field, and a truncated tail. Parse and projection reject every bad input on the same line; the reader fails at the bad bytes after N events, and a reader stopped after the first key never sees the fault (failure timing). A decoded value owns its text and outlives its source (no borrowed lifetimes; no lazy decode).

cards.title: Iterator capabilities survive adaptation: size_hint, fuse, by_ref, peek, back, remainder and copy
cards.body:
Destination: Iterable and its adapters carry verified capability facts (exact or bounded size, fused end, borrowed driving, lookahead, back reads, unread remainder, copyable position) through adaptation and type erasure, without a public iterator hierarchy or mandatory dynamic allocation. An upper bound is never labelled exact.

Why it matters: generic code needs these facts to be fast and correct; a helper name alone proves nothing.

Decisions: D-ITER-SIZE1=A, D-ITER-FUSED1=A, D-ITER-BORROW1=A, D-ITER-BACK1=A, D-ITER-LOOKAHEAD1=A, D-ITER-FAILCONSUME1=A, D-ITER-INTEROP1=A, D-ITER-EXACTGROUP1=A, D-ITER-REMAINDER1=A, D-ITER-COPY1=A, D-ITER-ENDLESS1=A.

Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md (finding iter-f005).

Moved out 2026-11-15: borrowed views (c25-c35) to #6871; lazy demand, flatten, intersperse, replay and cycle (c18, c36-c44, c46, c47) to the lazy adapters card.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Carry verified iterator capability facts through the existing Iterable/Iterator protocol, adapters and storage representations, without a public iterator hierarchy or mandatory dynamic allocation. Build the three ratified slices now:
- **D-ITER-SIZE1=A:** one runtime `size_hint()` pair; equal bounds convey exactness. There is no ExactRemaining hierarchy, no `remaining_len()` sibling and no runtime `@remaining`.
- **D-ITER-FUSED1=A:** a checked `fused` capability fact plus `fuse()`, which latches the first true end.
- **D-ITER-BORROW1=A:** `by_ref()` borrowed driving that reuses View/ViewMut provenance and sema overlap checks.

The open ballots D-ITER-BACK1 (reverse and mixed-end reads) and D-ITER-REPLAY1 each gate only their own slice.

## Current state
- The public `Iter` has no `size_hint`, `fuse` or `by_ref`: there are no rows in `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet`.
- The host uses `size_hint` only internally (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/FSIoEnvOsTesting.rs:453`).
- `JetIter` boxes a forward iterator. `ViewIter` and the user `Iterator` hooks (`Examples/features/collections/iter_hook.jet`) exist.
- Merged from #3336: a fused iterator never yields after its first end. Type erasure, `map` and driver loops never tag a source as fused. Async not-ready and channel `Empty` stay distinct from end (coordinate #3343), and nothing fuses silently.
- Canonical handoff (#3398): use #3325's checked operation facts, and keep the exact-size, double-ended, fused and remainder guarantees separate.

## Changes
1. Jet compiler:
   - `Collections.jet`: add `size_hint() -> (lower: Int, upper: Int?)` (non-advancing), `fuse() -> Iter<T>` and `by_ref()`. Adapters propagate conservative bounds (`map` keeps them; `filter` sets lower to 0; `take(n)` clamps; overflow sets upper to `None`) and the `fused` fact.
   - `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Ownership`: `by_ref` creates a loan on the source owner. Overlapping mutation is rejected with the existing overlap code, and the remainder stays usable after the loan ends.
   - Add ops in `TIR.jet`, with routes in `BuiltinMethods.jet`.
2. Host mirror:
   - `crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs` and the TIR lowering.
   - Prelude `JetIter` exposes `size_hint`, a `JetFuse` wrapper (one wrapper for non-fused sources) and `by_ref` over `&mut`.
   - The JIT rows and the MIREval arms.
3. Docs: `Docs/spec/reference/core-library.md` and a disposition row per stable Rust inventory entry (criterion 1). BACK1 and REPLAY1 rows follow the ratified D-ITER-BACK1=A and D-ITER-REPLAY1=A.

## Proof
- New `Examples/features/collections/iter_capabilities.jet` covers exact, bounded and unknown hints; a non-advancing query; a dishonest user hint that stays safe; overflow; a `fuse()` over a source that resumes after an empty poll; and `by_ref().take(2)` followed by reading the remainder.
  - `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=collections/iter_capabilities.jet Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
  - `JET_1216_STEM=collections/iter_capabilities Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev_tier_parity collections_memory_and_streams_match_interpreter_jit_and_aot` passes.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/iter_by_ref_overlap.jet Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` shows the mutation-while-borrowed rejection.

## Batch
`batch-host-runtime` (iter cluster, with sema loan checks).

## Dependencies
None for the three ratified slices. The reverse/mixed-end slice waits on D-ITER-BACK1 (recommended A) and replay on D-ITER-REPLAY1. No speed claim.
cards.checkSteps:
1. Each stable Rust inventory row has a semantic Jet disposition, including positive and negative capability bounds.
2. Mixed front/back consumption never duplicates an item and preserves the remaining range.
3. Exact-size operations are unavailable or explicitly fallible when only bounds are known; overflow cannot produce a false exact length.
4. A permanently exhausted wrapper remains exhausted, while a source that can resume after an empty poll is not mislabeled fused.
5. The representation and lowering preserve these facts without a separate public iterator hierarchy or mandatory dynamic allocation.

cards.title: One checked operation contract for collections and execution engines
cards.body:
Publish one authoritative operation contract for collection readers.

Names do not reveal eager versus lazy work, source ownership, callback order, error handling or buffering. Rust and Jet use some identical names for different contracts.

Document each existing public operation from its authoritative contract; feed existing generated API/docs and explain surfaces from the same semantic facts. Include corrected all/any teaching and link READ-F02/READ-F12, not another mutation-repair mechanism.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f013. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

The exact final per-row contract is retained in target-mine-playlist-20260911/analyses/iterators/stable-capability-map.json. This card owns its named delta only. Current-source runtime is NOT RUN; frozen e841 receipts remain historical.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-ONE-OPERATIONS1=A (ratified 2026-09-13) in the self-hosted compiler. Author one checked operation-contract row per collection/Iter operation and derive every repeated view from it: arity and access, callback types, result types, TBuiltinOp/TClosureOp selection, docs, completion and explain. Remove the replaced tables in one cutover. Keep D-CORE-EAGER1/2=A and the LAST ties from #2298.

## Current state
- The operation facts are split across four parallel `if method == …` tables in `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet`:
  - arity and access in `sema_collection_method_contract` (`:136-282`);
  - callback and argument types in `sema_collection_method_argument_type` (`:301-420`);
  - result types in `sema_collection_method_result_type` (`:423-667`);
  - operation selection in `sema_collection_method_operation` (`:669-924`).
- Each new Iter method (#3315, #3333, #3334, #3371 and others) must currently touch all four.
- Core call facts also live in `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/CoreCalls.jet` (565 lines) and `CoreCallRows.jet` (2011 lines). Their consumers are `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Collections.jet`, `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/BuiltinMethods.jet` and `ClosureMethods.jet`, and `Compiler/JetEval/Source/Routes`.
- The host kernels (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Collections.rs`, `Prelude/Core.jet`) are retained runtime. The rows reference them without re-describing them.
- The archived `crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs` and `Syntax/core_calls.rs` are reference only, and this card does not edit them.
- The finding is at Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f013 (READ-F02/READ-F12).

## Changes
1. `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet`:
   - Define one `CollectionOperationRow`: receiver kinds, access, arity, callback shape, result projection, TIR op, eager/lazy timing, callback count/order, stop-item consumption, failure channel, empty result, buffering, and a status of current, proposed or source-only.
   - Author every existing operation as a row.
   - Rewrite the four functions as lookups over the rows, then delete the `if` chains.
2. Cut every consumer over in the same pass: JetSema `Calls/Collections.jet`, JetCodegen `BuiltinMethods.jet`/`ClosureMethods.jet` (route rows keyed from the operation row), JetEval `Routes`, and the Web/JIT route inventories in Compiler/. Remove the replaced Path, owned-adapter and inclusion inventories.
3. Generate the Core reference operation table and the explain/completion text from the rows, through the existing `Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs` pipeline.
   - Correct the all/any teaching: empty `all` is true and empty `any` is false.
   - Rewrite `Docs/spec/reference/core-library.md:289-320` from the generated table.
4. Add `Examples/features/collections/operation_contract.jet` with the criteria cells. The remainder-continuation cell uses the #3315 `next`.
5. Criteria 1-6 and 7-12 duplicate each other (the pre-retarget and retargeted wording). Closing 7-12 closes 1-6.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.
- `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs --check` passes.
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden collections/operation_contract` passes on O0, O1 and O2.
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden collections/` passes, as a regression check that every existing collections golden is unchanged.

## Batch
`batch-jetc-sema`: JetFoundation tables consumed by JetSema first, then codegen and eval.

## Dependencies
#3315 is needed only for the remainder-continuation cell and can land in the same batch. Land this row refactor first within the batch: the new-method cards (#3315, #3333, #3334, #3371, #3329, #3354) then add rows, not four table edits.
